source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: Then, having conquered Yama, the chief among the gods, Ravana, who boasted of his prowess in battle, indeed saw his own companions.
verses.2: Then, having seen Ravana, whose body was drenched in blood and shattered by blows, the demons indeed approached him auspiciously.
verses.3: After Ravana had consoled them and celebrated their victory, Maricha and the other chiefs all boarded the Pushpaka chariot.
verses.4: Then, proceeding to Rasatala, he entered the ocean, which was inhabited by hosts of Daityas and Nagas and well-protected by Varuna.
verses.5: Having gone to the city of Bhogavati, protected by Vasuki, and having brought the Nagas under his control, he, delighted, proceeded to the gem-studded city.
verses.6: There lived the Nivātakavachas, Daityas who had obtained boons, and Ravana, having approached them, challenged them to battle.
verses.7: All those Daityas were indeed very mighty, powerful, equipped with various weapons, and overjoyed and fierce in battle.
verses.8: The enraged Rakshasas and Danavas fiercely pierced each other with spears, tridents, thunderbolts, sharp-edged spears, swords, and axes.
verses.9: As they continued to fight, more than a year passed, yet neither side achieved victory nor suffered complete destruction.
verses.10: Then, the imperishable god Brahma, the lord of the three worlds, quickly arrived there, seated in his magnificent aerial chariot.
verses.11: Having stopped that act of war involving the Nivatakavachas, the wise grandfather Brahma spoke meaningful words.
verses.12: Indeed, this Ravana cannot be conquered in battle by gods and asuras, nor can you (Nivatakavachas) be led to destruction even by gods and Danavas.
verses.13: Friendship with you Rakshasas is agreeable, and there is no doubt that all interests of friends are undivided.
verses.14: Then, Ravana established a friendship with the Nivātakavachas, with fire as witness, and became delighted at that time.
verses.15: Ravana then resided there for a year, treated properly and justly by them, receiving affection as if he were in his own city.
verses.16: Then, having mastered a full hundred magic arts, Ravana wandered through the netherworld in search of the city of Varuna, the lord of waters.
verses.17: Then, having gone to the city named Ashmanagara, which was inhabited by the Kalakeyas, Ravana killed the exceedingly strong Kalakeyas there.
verses.18: Then, Ravana cut off Shurpanakha's husband, his mighty and exceedingly strong brother-in-law named Vidyujjihva, who was a Rakshasa licking (blood/wounds) with his tongue in battle, with his sword.
verses.19: Having conquered him, he killed four hundred demons in an instant.
verses.20: Then, the lord of rakshasas saw the divine abode of Varuna, which resembled white clouds and shone like Mount Kailasa.
verses.21: There he saw the divine cow Surabhi, standing and continuously flowing milk, from whose abundant milk flow the ocean named Kshiroda originated.
verses.22: There Ravana saw the ocean, the best source of cows, bulls, and excellent things, from which the cool-rayed moon, the maker of night, originated.
verses.23: Great sages known as foam-drinkers subsist by depending on this ocean, and it is also where nectar and Svadhā, the offering for ancestors, originated.
verses.24: Ravana, having circumambulated the exceedingly wonderful Surabhi, whom people in the world call by that name, then proceeded.
verses.25: He then entered a very dreadful place, guarded by various forces, and there he saw Varuna's excellent abode, which was filled with hundreds of streams, resembled an autumn cloud, and was always joyful.
verses.26: Then, having killed the commanders of the army in battle and being struck by them, Ravana said to the warriors, "Let the king (Varuna) be quickly informed."
verses.27: "Ravana, desirous of battle, has arrived; let battle be given to him, or else, with folded hands, say 'I am conquered' if you have no fear."
verses.28: At this moment, the enraged sons and grandsons of the great-souled Varuna, including Gau and Pushkara, came out.
verses.29: Endowed with valorous qualities and surrounded by their own forces, they yoked their chariots, which moved at will, shining with brilliant splendor.
verses.30: Then, a terrible and hair-raising battle ensued between the sons of Varuna, the lord of waters, and the intelligent Ravana.
verses.31: And by the very powerful ministers of the Rakshasa Dashagriva, that entire army of Varuna was destroyed in a moment.
verses.32: Then, seeing their own army afflicted by a shower of arrows in battle, the sons of Varuna retreated from the fight.
verses.33: Indeed, they, who were on the ground, having seen Ravana in the Pushpaka chariot, quickly ascended into the sky with their swift-moving chariots.
verses.34: After obtaining an equal position in the sky, a great and tumultuous battle ensued among them, resembling the fierce combat between gods and demons.
verses.35: Then, having turned Ravana away in battle with their fire-like arrows, they were satisfied and roared various sounds.
verses.36: Then, the enraged hero Mahodara, seeing his king humiliated, abandoned all fear of death and, desirous of battle, looked towards the enemy.
verses.37: In that fierce battle, those who moved at will and resembled the wind were indeed struck by Mahodara with his mace and fell to the earth.
verses.38: Having killed hundreds of warriors and horses belonging to the sons of Varuna, Mahodara quickly let out a great roar upon seeing them standing dismounted from their chariots.
verses.39: Mahodara struck down their chariots, which, along with their horses and slain charioteers, fell to the ground.
verses.40: But those brave sons of the great-souled Varuna, having abandoned their chariots, stood in the sky and were not distressed due to their inherent power.
verses.41: Enraged, they made their bows ready, pierced Mahodara, and together attacked Ravana in battle.
verses.42: Greatly enraged, they tore him apart with very terrible arrows, released from their bows and resembling thunderbolts, just as clouds tear apart a great mountain.
verses.43: Then, the enraged Ravana, appearing like the fire of destruction, struck their vital spots with very dreadful showers of arrows.
verses.44: Then, by him alone, the foot-soldiers suddenly began to collapse under the impact of various maces and hundreds of spears.
verses.45: The irresistible Ravana, positioned above them, hurled down sharp-edged spears, lances, 'hundred-killers', and javelins upon them.
verses.46: Those brave foot-soldiers, struck down, scattered and fled like sixty-year-old elephants that have fallen into a deep mud-pit.
verses.47: Seeing his very mighty enemies (literally 'sons') collapsing and distressed, Ravana roared with joy like a great thundercloud.
verses.48: Then, the Rakshasa Ravana, having uttered great roars, struck down the followers of Varuna (Devas) with showers of various weapons, just like a cloud pours down torrents of rain.
verses.49: Then, all of them, defeated and fallen to the ground, were quickly brought back into their homes by their own men from the battlefield.
verses.50: Then the demon Ravana said to them, "Let this be announced to Varuna."
verses.51: Then a minister of Varuna named Prahasta (or Prahasa) said to Ravana, "Indeed, the great king, the lord of waters Varuna, has gone to the world of Brahma."
verses.52: Varuna, whom you challenge in battle, has gone to hear Gandharva music; therefore, O hero, what is the use of your vain exertion when the king is absent, and those princes who were present here have already been defeated?
verses.53: Having heard that, the lord of demons Ravana, proclaiming his own name and uttering a joyful roar, indeed departed from Varuna's abode.
verses.54: Having arrived by a certain path, the demon Ravana returned by that very path, flying through the sky towards Lanka. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रयोविंशः सर्गः ।। 23 ।। Thus ends the twenty-third sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
